title: Legacy Data Cleanup
tagline: Tools for finding and fixing decades of messy records, with a person approving the fixes
summary: The county was moving from an old DOS system to a new web app, and a lot of the old data came over broken. Notes were split across rows, words were stuck together, and values ended up in the wrong place. At my 2026 internship I built tools that find these problems, suggest fixes, and let a person approve each one.

sections.heading: Why the data was messy
body: In the old system, people typed long notes into narrow fixed-width fields that wrapped onto the next row. When it was imported, those line breaks disappeared, so words got glued together and comments got chopped into pieces. The tricky part is that some weird-looking values are actually correct, so you can't just fix everything that looks odd.

sections.heading: Finding the problems
body: First I wrote scripts that scan every column and flag what looks wrong, without changing anything. A rare value in a column full of repeats is probably a typo, while a rare value in a column of IDs is normal.

sections.heading: Using AI carefully
body: The flagged records went to an AI in small batches, with instructions for how to read the table and exactly what format to answer in. Anything that came back incomplete or didn't match its batch got rejected. Then a review app showed each suggestion next to the original cells, and a person approved, edited or dismissed it.
codeBlocks:
LEGACY RECORDS
      ↓
PROFILE + DETECT  →  suspicious cells and fragments
      ↓
JSON BATCHES      →  AI reconstruction and review
      ↓
HUMAN REVIEW      →  approve · edit · flag · dismiss
      ↓
STAGED CHANGES    →  verify · back up · apply

sections.heading: Fixing the easy ones automatically
body: One kind of problem was purely mechanical: a missing space where a line wrapped. For those I made a separate fixer that's only allowed to add or remove spaces, never change a letter or a number. If even one change broke that rule, the whole run stopped. A dry run on all the data found 21,616 fixes and zero rule breaks.

sections.heading: How I built it
body: Most of this code was written by AI. My part was explaining where the data came from, giving it real examples, deciding what the steps should be, and checking its work. Since the AI wrote so much of it, the strict checks and the human review are what made me trust the results.
